theme: Housing and rent inflation nowcasts (Zillow observed rent, Apartment List, Fed rent nowcasts), new-tenant rent index, shelter CPI nowcasting repos
queries_run: gh search repos "new tenant rent index"
gh search repos "zillow observed rent index"
gh search repos "new tenant repeat rent"

candidates.name: shadow-rent-index
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/Selenium ETL pipeline (MIT license) that scrapes weekly rental listings from real-estate platforms for targeted zip codes in Madison, WI only, cleans with pandas (regex price cleaning, room-type extraction, outlier removal) and loads to a PostgreSQL time-series DB. No data committed to the repo itself; requires running the scraper (undetected-chromedriver) on a schedule to populate any history. Single small metro, 1 contributor, updated May 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates a 'zero-lag shadow rent index' methodology (listing-based nowcast ahead of official CPI shelter) that could in principle be re-pointed at broader geography, but as-is it is single-city and holds no usable committed data.
candidates.size_hint: no committed dataset; DB populated only by running scraper

candidates.name: rm (repeat-sales rent index)
candidates.what_it_holds: web2py application implementing a repeat-sales regression method to build a rental price index, tracking the same properties over time. Repo includes some reference data used for the calculation but the README does not specify whether production rent-listing data is committed or geography/date range covered (undocumented, 3 stars, last touched 2022).
candidates.why_useful: A working repeat-sales index construction method could be adapted to any committed or newly-collected rent panel to build a new-tenant-style rent index as an ABNB substitute-cost/backdrop indicator, but is unmaintained and its data scope is unclear.
candidates.size_hint: small reference dataset bundled with repo, size unstated

candidates.name: vesta-rental-index
candidates.what_it_holds: Very new repo (updated 2026-09-13, 1 star) named 'Vesta Rental Index'; gh search returned no description beyond the name, so scope/data-commit status unverified. Flagged for a follow-up look rather than confirmed content.
candidates.why_useful: Recency (created/updated the day before this scout ran) makes it worth a human glance in case it is a new rent-index build with committed data; unverified.
candidates.size_hint: unknown, not inspected beyond search metadata

candidates.name: ZORI
candidates.what_it_holds: Small personal repo working with Zillow's own publicly-downloadable Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI) CSVs (metro/zip-level, smoothed and seasonally adjusted, monthly, 2015+, direct from zillow.com/research/data). Repo itself likely just re-hosts or notebooks against the same public Zillow file already available directly from Zillow (no scrape needed), so treat the primary source (Zillow Research data page) as the actual holding.
candidates.why_useful: ZORI is the standard high-frequency, city-level asking-rent series used to proxy shelter-cost pressure on consumers/hosts; useful as a macro backdrop control for ABNB nights/ADR regressions, but obtainable directly from Zillow without this repo.
candidates.size_hint: Zillow's public ZORI CSV, several MB
candidates.license: unspecified (data itself is Zillow's, publicly downloadable, non-commercial redistribution terms apply)

candidates.name: RentPricePredict
candidates.what_it_holds: ML model for predicting rental prices trained on Zillow's public ZORI data; again points back to the same publicly-downloadable Zillow source rather than adding new proprietary data.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — modeling exercise over an already-public series; no new data.

candidates.name: rentmap
candidates.what_it_holds: Python visualization of Zillow Rent Index data (map-based); again sources from Zillow's public download, no independent dataset.

candidates.name: mw-mietspiegel-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 licensed API for Berlin's official Mietspiegel (rent index/comparative local rent), returning Wohnlage (residential-status classification) and comparative rent for Berlin addresses for the 2017/2019 editions. Actively-flavored municipal rent-benchmark API, Germany-specific.
candidates.why_useful: Only relevant if the pitch needs a European (Berlin) rent-cost benchmark for cross-market ADR/rent-substitution analysis; not US and narrow in scope, but is a real, structured, licensed dataset+API rather than a toy notebook.
candidates.size_hint: API-served lookup tables, not a bulk file

notes: This theme returned almost nothing purpose-built for shelter-CPI/new-tenant-rent nowcasting on GitHub: zero hits for 'new tenant rent index', 'shelter cpi nowcast', 'rent nowcast', 'CPI shelter forecast', 'Cleveland Fed rent', and 'housing inflation nowcast' (all returned empty result sets from gh search repos). The only non-empty buckets were generic 'Zillow Rent Index' student/portfolio projects (dozens of near-duplicate notebooks re-plotting the same public ZORI CSV — excluded as boilerplate except the handful listed) and one Madison-WI-only scraper (shadow-rent-index) plus one unmaintained repeat-sales-index web2py app (rm). No repo was found that mirrors or nowcasts Apartment List's rent index, the NY Fed/Cleveland Fed new-tenant repeat rent series, or BLS shelter CPI construction — that class of work appears to live in academic code (FRB working paper replication packages, often not on GitHub) or proprietary vendor tooling, not indexed public GitHub repos discoverable by these keywords. Recommend a human check https://github.com/rodafa/vesta-rental-index directly (created the day before this scout, no description returned by search) and consider that this theme may be better served by going straight to the primary public sources (Zillow Research ZORI/ZHVI direct download, Apartment List Rent Estimates report + data page, Cleveland Fed New Tenant Repeat Rent Index page, BLS CPI microdata) rather than GitHub mirrors, since none of the repos found add data beyond what those primary sources already publish for free. Used more than the nominal 6 gh search calls (11 total, no rate-limit errors encountered) because early queries returned empty; stopped once results started repeating (same Zillow-notebook cluster) and switched to WebFetch for verification of two candidates instead of further searching.
